lessons.title: 9. 气体、液体和固体的结构

nearbyText:
A liquid can be compared to a crowd whose members keep changing places, and a crystal to an orderly group whose members move around their assigned positions;
this analogy only illustrates differences in arrangement and motion.

In the periodic crystals discussed here, particles' average positions have a long-range periodic arrangement that can be described by a spatial lattice.
Amorphous solids lack this long-range periodic arrangement, so not all solids should be treated as crystals.

Table salt (Figure $11$), diamond (Figure $12$), and magnesium (Figure $13$) are the source's examples of crystal lattices;
the particles are ions in salt and atoms in diamond and magnesium.
The ordered internal arrangement can produce regular geometric faces under suitable growth conditions (Figure $14$), but not every piece of a crystal has a complete regular outer shape.
